t: For an additional amount for “Operation and Maintenance, Defense-Wide,” $46,200,000: Provided, That such amount is designated by Congress as an emergency requirement pursuant to section 251(b)(2)(D)(i) of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985, as amended.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriations provision that funds Defense-Wide operation and maintenance and designates the amount as an emergency requirement. The only tempting hook is the reference to a designation by Congress, but Congress is inside the federal government and no outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue.
fable.s: Provided, That such amount is designated by Congress as an emergency requirement

qwen_block.w: This section is a congressional appropriation provision that allocates funds and designates them as an emergency requirement. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process involving parties outside the federal government. Congress is an internal part of the federal government, and the text contains no mechanism for public or external participation.
qwen_block.s: For an additional amount for “Operation and Maintenance, Defense-Wide,” $46,200,000: Provided, That such amount is designated by Congress as an emergency requirement pursuant to section 251(b)(2)(D)(i) of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985, as amended.

opus.w: This section only provides extra funding for "Operation and Maintenance, Defense-Wide" and designates it as an emergency requirement under the Balanced Budget Act. No outside party (state, tribe, expert, company or the public) is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. Congress's emergency designation happens entirely inside the federal government, so it is not participation.
opus.b: The only tempting reading is that Congress designating the money as an emergency requirement counts as a federal decision with procedural steps. It doesn't. Congress is inside the federal government, and the section involves no one from outside it.
